question: Jackson’s paintbrush makes a narrow strip with a width of \(6.5\) millimeters. Jackson has enough paint to make a strip \(25\) meters long. How many square centimeters of paper could Jackson cover with paint?
solution:
The painted strip is a rectangle. Expressing both dimensions in centimeters lets us obtain its area in square centimeters by multiplying length and width.

Since \(1\) centimeter equals \(10\) millimeters, the width is
\[
6.5\div10=0.65\text{ cm}.
\]
Since \(1\) meter equals \(100\) centimeters, the length is
\[
25\cdot100=2500\text{ cm}.
\]
The area Jackson can cover is therefore
\[
2500\cdot0.65=\boxed{1625}\text{ square centimeters},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
